explanation: Raw GRU candidate n for unit 26. Timing explains most of its variance (R^2 0.96: about +0.8 at D1, -0.99 at GO, +0.97 at D2). The variance left over is almost all at D1. There the unit drops when the previous trial was unrewarded, most strongly when that trial reached S1 (fitted about -0.3; a1 S1 u residual -0.47, a2 S1 u -0.38). It falls further for each extra unrewarded trial in a row: a second loss adds about -0.36 and a third about -0.3, so long loss streaks push D1 to about -0.8 to -1.6. The drop also grows later in the episode. A rewarded last trial raises it (+0.15). An unrewarded S1 visit two trials back still lowers it. A graded tanh of the D1 policy logit adds a little (lower when the logit leans toward a2). At D2 it dips slightly on a1 -> S2 rare trials. GO is flat. Test R^2 beyond timing is 0.587 against the all-cue ceiling of 0.62, so about 95% of the ceiling. No future variables are used; one term uses a model output (the policy logit), and the reward/state terms alone give about 0.52 to 0.56 on dev. The hidden good state and since_rev add nothing. Worst misses are long a2 S1 R unrewarded stretches whose loss history starts before the 5-trial window.

issues: I reproduced the reported test R^2 beyond timing of 0.5865, against the all-cue ceiling of 0.62. Dropping one term at a time, every claimed effect holds on test: tanh(choice) is worth 0.028 (0.559 without it), the loss-by-ep_trial growth 0.016 (0.570), the S1 loss two trials back 0.024 (0.563), the third-loss term 0.015 (0.572) and the D2 a1->S2 dip 0.013 (0.574). The reward and state terms alone score 0.546 on test, which matches the claimed 0.52-0.56.

The loss-run claim is too broad. The run terms ignore which state the last loss was at, so D1 after a2 S2 u is under-predicted by +0.126 and after a1 S2 u by +0.062 (they don't drop as far as predicted). Adding (phase==D1)*(prev_reward==0)*(prev_state==2)*(tv('reward',-2)==0) gets weight +0.40, which cancels most of the second-loss weight (-0.45). So a second loss in a row deepens the drop mainly when the last loss was at S1, and barely when it was at S2. With that term, test R^2 rises to 0.601.

The worst misses are the first D1 in a window (around -0.8 actual against about +0.6 to +0.8 predicted) and partial recovery after a reward that follows a loss run (about +0.5 against +0.8). Both come from loss history that started before the window. The explanation already names this, and a window-start term does not fix it (test 0.584).
Smaller leftover errors: D1 after a2 S1 r is over-predicted (-0.08) and D1 on the window's first trial (no previous trial in the window) is over-predicted (-0.06). Neither is a large class.
